headline: Medium interaction risk: shared-bus Pipecat can ingest PaddleOCR outputs, creating prompt-injection and cascading-error pathways; no direct evidence of a blocked bridge.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: PaddleOCR can process documents/images and Pipecat can consume text over stdin/stdout and shared-bus sessions. That creates a plausible bridge where OCR output is treated as instructions. No direct provenance or sanitization is documented, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF PaddleOCR output is forwarded into Pipecat without provenance tagging
IF Pipecat parses OCR text as conversational instructions
mitigations: Add a fixed delimiter and provenance label before passing OCR text
Strip imperative phrases from OCR output before ingestion
Route OCR output through a human review step for high-risk tasks
Disable stdin/stdout bridging for untrusted documents
requires-engineering: add schema validation between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: PaddleOCR touches documents and images, while Pipecat handles text, conversation state, analytics, and can call many third-party APIs. A shared-bus or pipeline could expose document contents to external services through Pipecat. The profiles do not show a hard isolation boundary, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF document text from PaddleOCR is sent into Pipecat services that call third-party APIs
IF the shared bus carries sensitive document content across instances
mitigations: Keep sensitive OCR jobs off Pipecat-connected flows
Use local-only Pipecat services for the pipeline
Redact PII before handoff from OCR to Pipecat
Turn off analytics/telemetry for sensitive runs
requires-engineering: enforce per-hop data classification checks

C_capability_conflict.rationale: PaddleOCR has allowlisted network egress and Pipecat also has allowlisted egress, but neither profile shows shared writable filesystem, git, or overlapping OAuth scopes. The main overlap is read/transform rather than conflicting writes, so blast radius is small.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write to the same mutable resource outside the shown profiles
mitigations: Separate output directories per agent
Avoid concurrent writes to shared files
Use a queue instead of direct shared-state mutation
Lock any downstream mutable resource
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level resource locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Pipecat can run multi-service voice and LLM pipelines, so it may treat PaddleOCR text as authoritative input. If OCR errors or injected text flow into downstream actions, Pipecat can amplify them across APIs or conversation state. The interaction is plausible in default pipelines, but not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF Pipecat uses PaddleOCR output as a source of facts without verification
IF downstream Pipecat services act on OCR-derived text
mitigations: Insert a verification step before downstream actions
Mark OCR output as untrusted in the prompt/context
Require confidence thresholds for extracted text
Log source attribution alongside each extracted fact
requires-engineering: add automated fact-checking gates

E_compliance.rationale: PaddleOCR processes documents and images, and Pipecat handles conversation state plus analytics/metrics with many external service integrations. If regulated document content is routed through Pipecat, retention and residency obligations can diverge. No specific certifications are listed, so uncertainty again favors the higher severity.
conditions: IF regulated documents or PII are passed from PaddleOCR into Pipecat services
IF Pipecat analytics or third-party APIs retain that data beyond policy
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from the pipeline
Disable analytics for regulated workloads
Minimize stored conversation state
Review vendor retention settings before deployment
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls
